resources.string: NexSense is an exploration and logging tool, not a professional building-safety, health or laboratory instrument. Phone sensors are not calibrated.

Hold the phone at the point, aim its top edge at a surface (wall, ceiling) and measure. Each measurement places a point at the first echo distance in the direction the phone faces and adds it to the 3D structure. The speaker is not directional, so wrong echoes are possible.
Pick a point with a position for the direction scan.
Plays short pulses; distance to surfaces comes from the delay between direct sound and echo (0.3–5 m). The speaker is not directional: the strongest echo is usually the nearest large surface.
The microphone could not be opened (another app may be using it).
The speaker could not play the signal.

Place the phone on a steady surface (table, tripod), keep the room quiet and do not touch it during measurement. The speaker plays short sounds and the microphone listens for echoes. Audio is processed in memory only.
Calibration offset %1$s dB: approximate dB SPL is saved too (unweighted).
No calibration: values are saved as dBFS (relative). Settings → Sound calibration gives approximate dB SPL.
Room modes for scan dimensions %1$s × %2$s × %3$s m:
Where the phone sits. Position is optional; leave empty if unknown.
No point selected; you can measure, but pick a point to save.
Set north: phone now points to project +y
Project north angle not set: magnetic north = project +y is assumed and the scan is marked \"unaligned\".
Results are saved to this point. If the point has a position, acoustic values appear there in the 3D scene.
Audio is never written to disk; only computed values are saved.
Plays a rising tone twice (~10 s). RT60 is computed in octave bands. Phone speakers are weak in bass; 125 Hz may be unreliable.
Speed of sound %1$s m/s (no temperature sensor; %2$s °C assumed).
Media volume is low; raise it above 70 percent for more reliable results.
Set a lower/upper limit per layer; points outside are listed.
Robust z-score from median and median absolute deviation, |z| > 3.5 (minimum points: %1$d). Could also be a measurement error; re-measuring on site is recommended.
Change between sessions at the same spot (≤0.5 m)
Pearson r for two layers measured at the same points. Correlation is not causation; a shared factor or spatial layout can also produce it.

Inverse distance weighting in the horizontal plane. Only cells closer than the given distance to a measurement are estimated; the rest stays empty. Shown as faint hatched cells, apart from measurements, in the scene and the report.
Measurement coverage, threshold alerts, unusual-value candidates, relations between layers and change over time. None of these is a definitive finding; they point at places worth a closer look.

Device-axis readings are rotated into the East-North-Up frame with the stored orientation matrix. Horizontal (H) and vertical (Z) components and the inclination do not depend on how the phone was held.
No two layers share enough measured points (minimum: %1$d).
Approximate, from the 2–98%% box of scan points (points: %1$d). Used for acoustic room modes.
An empty limit is not used. Values are in the layer\'s unit.
There is only one session. Re-measure the same places at another time to see change here.
Not enough texture; point at a more detailed area.
This device\'s GPU does not support the AR view.
Finding position… move the phone slowly.
The camera image is processed on the device only for motion tracking and is not recorded. Works best on textured surfaces in good light; on plain white walls tracking can be lost.
This phone does not support ARCore. Step counting is available: it is a rough estimate, and points are marked as \"estimated position\".
ARCore works out where the phone is from patterns in the camera image and motion sensors. The image is not recorded.
Saved points: %1$d · cloud: %2$d · planes: %3$d · path: %4$s m
ARCore could not start. Google Play Services for AR must be installed and up to date.

Where you press Start becomes the reference. As you walk, the phone saves a measurement point at every step interval with position, sensor values and orientation. When you finish, the point cloud, planes and path are added to the project.
The compass (magnetometer + accelerometer) could not be read; step mode does not work on this device.
Rough position from step counting and the compass. Error accumulates with every step; height is not measured, the holding height from settings is used. Points are drawn with a dashed ring.
Hold the phone in front of you with its top edge pointing where you walk, and walk with normal steps.
Camera image, audio and position are never sent anywhere; only measurement results are stored in the project.

Hold the phone at the start point with its top edge pointing to the project\'s forward (+y) direction. Where the phone is and where it points at that moment become the origin of the coordinate system.
… or start from an existing point:
A new measurement point is saved each time the phone moves this far. Smaller spacing means more detail but more data.

Next to a reference sound level meter, with a steady sound (e.g. pink noise or a fan), enter the meter\'s dB reading and measure. The difference is stored as an offset; the result is still approximate (no frequency weighting).

NexSense case file Project: %1$s Created: %2$s App version: %3$s
Contents: project JSON (importable), CSV (raw data), PDF report, PLY 3D model. Integrity: %4$s lists the SHA-256 of every file (e.g. \"sha256sum -c\"). NexSense is an exploration and logging tool, not a professional instrument.
All values in the demo project are made up and always shown with a “DEMO DATA” label. They never mix with your real projects.
Made-up sample data. Not a real measurement; for getting to know the app.
The file is not a NexSense project or is damaged.
The file is too large (50 MB max).
The data is inconsistent and was not saved (%1$s).
This file was made by a newer version of the app. Update the app first.
Enter x, y and z together, or leave all three empty.
A measurement unit is missing or wrong; nothing was saved.
CSV needs at least one sample.
Create a project for a space (room, office, workshop), then add measurement points from the Live screen. You can first browse the clearly labelled demo project.
Collect measurement points with your phone\'s sensors and explore them layer by layer in a 3D scene relative to your own reference point. Measured, estimated and unknown are always shown apart.
Could not open the install confirmation.
The update is incompatible with this installation (the signature may differ).
Not enough free storage on the device.
Only measured points are coloured; the space between means “not measured”. With “Estimate” on, faint hatched cells are IDW estimates, not measurements.
%1$s: no data. No measurements were taken for this layer.
Measured points: %1$d. Hollow grey ring: not measured at this point.
No colour layer: points are shown by position only.

In auto measure you type no coordinates: start and walk; the phone tracks its own position and saves points itself. In acoustic mode the phone sits still and measures distance and room acoustics with sound.
Axes are in the phone\'s own frame (facing the screen: x right, y up, z out of the screen). Values are shown in the units the device reports, unconverted.
You can watch the values; open a project to record them.
Use “Add measurement point” on the Live screen to save the current sensor values.
Microphone permission was denied. Other sensors keep working.
The microphone could not be opened (another app may be using it).
Microphone permission is needed to measure sound level. Audio is not recorded; only the level is computed on the device.
Acoustic measurement saved to the point.
%1$s project file(s) could not be read; they were left untouched.
Open or create a project on the Home screen.
No sensor samples at this point (note only).
Bass analysis needs an external speaker (Phase 3).
Missing on most phones; external sensor support comes in Phase 3.
Low dynamic range; result is approximate.
Magnets and metal inside the phone affect the value; hold the phone the same way when comparing.
dBFS relative to full scale; uncalibrated, not dB SPL. Audio is never recorded.
Mid-frequency reverberation could not be measured (noise or low volume).
The phone speaker cannot play enough bass; 125 Hz is unreliable.
Only a real ambient temperature sensor is used. Battery or CPU temperature is not ambient temperature and is never substituted. Most phones lack this sensor; external sensor support comes in Phase 3.
RMS of gravity-free linear acceleration over the last ~100 samples (derived).
Saved with each measurement point. Magnetic disturbance can skew the azimuth.
Describe the physical point that is the origin (e.g. “bottom-left corner of the living room door, floor”). x goes right from it, y forward, z up.
This project contains DEMO DATA: values are made up, not real measurements.
Faint hatched cells are IDW estimates (cells: %1$d, max distance %2$s m); they are not measurements.

Sensor values are stored in the units the device reports, unconverted; phone sensors are not calibrated. Position: manual, ARCore visual-inertial tracking (arcore, ~cm) or step counting (pdr, rough estimate). Vibration: linear-acceleration RMS. Sound: dBFS; approximate dB SPL if an offset is set. Reverberation: exponential sweep, Schroeder T20 → RT60. Echo distance: matched-filter sonar. Anomaly: robust z > 3.5. Relation: Pearson r. Unmeasured places are never shown as measured.
Perspective view; points coloured by the %1$s layer. Grey ring: not measured in this layer.
Top-down plan (1 m grid). Measured range %1$s – %2$s %3$s. Blue line: walking path; teal: detected planes; grey: point cloud.
For auto measure on phones without ARCore. Step length directly affects position accuracy.
The microphone is requested only when you start a sound measurement, the camera only for ARCore auto measure. Image and audio are never recorded. Location (GPS) and Bluetooth are not used.
Point “%1$s” and its samples will be deleted.
Metres from the project\'s reference point: x right, y forward, z up. GPS is unreliable indoors, so position is entered by hand.
If left empty, position is saved as “unknown” and the point is not shown in the 3D scene. No fake coordinates are made up.
Data stays on this device. The app never sends measurement data to any server; export only writes where you choose.
“%1$s” will be deleted permanently (measurement points: %2$d). You may want to export it as JSON first.

CSV writes one row per measurement component: time, project, point, sensor, value, unit, coordinates, source and quality. Missing values are empty cells. JSON stores the whole project in an importable form.
Opens a previously exported .nexsense.json file. If the same project exists it is not overwritten; a copy is added.
Open a project to export. Import is always available.

PDF report: summary, scene images, layer tables, analysis and methods. 3D model (PLY): point cloud, planes and coloured measurement points (MeshLab, CloudCompare, Blender). Case file: everything in one ZIP with a SHA-256 integrity list.
Sensors run only while the Live screen is open. High rate is better for vibration but uses more battery.
This scan\'s point cloud, planes and path will be deleted. Measurement points are kept.
A session opens automatically with the first point.

The case file of “%1$s” (measurement points: %2$d, samples: %3$d, scan points: %4$d, including PDF and 3D model) will be sent to the app you choose. NexSense itself never sends data to any server; you choose where the file goes.
Only points with a known position are placed in the scene. Points without a position: %1$d. Easiest is Auto measure: start and walk.
No points to show in the scene
ESTIMATE: hatched cells are not measurements (cells: %1$d)
3D scene; measurement points: %1$d. Drag to rotate, pinch to zoom, tap to select.
